newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Shenzhen not to become tariff-free port.
newsitem.headline: China's Shenzhen not to become tariff-free port.

text.p: China's southern boomtown of Shenzhen, which borders Hong Kong, will not become a tariff-free port after Beijing resumes sovereignty over the British colony this year, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.

The city in Guangdong province would remain a special economic zone after July 1, when Hong Kong is to return to China after more than 150 years of British rule, the newspaper quoted Xu Yaping, deputy director of the State Council's Special Economic Zone Office, as saying.
"China's modernisation drive will not need another free port, and Shenzhen cannot afford to become the next one after Hong Kong," Xu said.
Turning Shenzhen into a free port would effectively cut the city off from the huge domestic market by making its products more expensive, Xu said.

Shenzhen also would be unlikely to stand up to the intense international competition it would face as a free port, the newspaper quoted Chen Bingcai, an analyst with the State Planning Commission, as saying.
Shenzhen and other special economic zones would continue to serve as test grounds for new economic policies, Xu said.
